accepted.question_text: For the stochastic scheduling model on an unreliable machine governed by the coupled equations d/dt p0(x,t) + d/dx p0(x,t) = -(lambda(x)+mu(x)) p0(x,t) and d/dt p1(x,t) + d/dx p1(x,t) = -eta(x) p1(x,t), with boundary conditions p0(0,t) = delta(t) + integral from 0 to infinity of p1(x,t) eta(x) dx and p1(0,t) = integral from 0 to infinity of p0(x,t) lambda(x) dx, and initial data p0(x,0) = delta(x), p1(x,0) = 0, determine the explicit time-dependent solution in the general non-constant case lambda(x), mu(x), eta(x). Equivalently, determine the Laplace inverse transforms of the formulas for p1-hat(x,s) and p0-hat(x,s) so that the full time-domain solution can be written down.

evidence.quote: But we can not obtain the Laplace inverse transform, that is to say, we could not give the explicit expression of the time-dependent solution for general case.

If we can determine the Laplace inverse transform of (3.13) and (3.14), then we can get the time-dependent solution of the equation system (1.1)-(1.5). But, until today we have not discovered an efficient method to resolve this problem.

accepted.question_text: For Linton's 1976 two-unit parallel redundant system with state probabilities q0,i(x,t), q1,i(x,t), and q2,j(x,t), where one unit has k failure stages, the other has m repair phases, the boundary condition includes q0,1(0,t) = integral from 0 to infinity of q1,1(x,t) g(x) dx + delta(t), lambda > 0 and mu > 0 are system parameters, g(x) is the repair rate of unit 1, and f(x) is the failure rate of unit 2, determine whether the PDE model is well posed and determine the asymptotic behavior of its time-dependent solution when g(x) and f(x) are non-constant functions.

evidence.quote: Where (x, t) in [0, infinity) x [0, infinity); p0,i(x, t) (1 <= i <= k) is the probability that at moment t, no units are down, unit 2 is in the ith stage of failure, and unit 1 has been operating for an amount of time x; p1,i(x, t) (1 <= i <= k) is the probability that at moment t, unit 1 is down, unit 2 is in the ith stage of failure and an amount of x, has already been spent on the current repair of unit 1; p2,j(x, t) (1 <= j <= m) are the probability that at moment t, unit 2 is down, unit 2 is in the jth phase of repair, and unit 1 has been operating for an amount of time x; lambda > 0 and mu > 0 are parameters of unit 1 and unit 2 respectively; g(x) is the repair rate of unit 1; f(x) is the failure rate of unit 2, delta(.) is the Dirac-delta function.
When g(x) and f(x) are non-constants, well-posedness of the above model and asymptotic behavior of its time-dependent solution have not been obtained until today.

accepted.question_text: For the 1993 model with state variables p0,i(x,t), p1,i(x,t), p2(x,u,t), p3(x,t), and p4(x,u,t), representing a two-unit parallel system with operating, repair, waiting-for-repair, and suspended-repair states; with a1 > 0 the Erlang-distribution parameter, a2(x) the repair rate of unit 1, b1(x) the life rate, b2(x) the repair rate of unit 2, and boundary data including p0,1(0,t) = integral from 0 to infinity of p1,1(x,t) b2(x) dx + delta(t), determine whether the PDE model is well posed and determine the asymptotic behavior of its time-dependent solution.

evidence.quote: Where (x, u, t) in [0, infinity) x [0, infinity) x [0, infinity); p0,i(x, t) is the probability that at time t two units are operating and the operating unit 1 is in phase i, and the age of unit 2 is x; p1,i(x, t) is the probability that at time t unit 1 is operating, the operating phase is i and unit 2 is being repaired and the elapsed time of the failed unit 2 is x; p2(x, u, t) is the probability that at time t unit 2 is operating and unit 1 is being repaired, the elapsed repair time of the failed unit 1 is x, and the age of unit 2 is u; p3(x, t) is the probability that at time t unit 1 is being repaired and unit 2 is waiting for repair, and the elapsed repair time of the failed unit 1 is x; p4(x, u, t) is the probability that at time t unit 1 is being repaired and unit 2 is in suspended repair, and the elapsed repair time of the failed unit 1 is x and the elapsed time of the failed unit 2 is u; a1 > 0 is a constant parameter of the Erlang distribution; a2(x) is the repair rate of unit 1; b1(x) is the life rate; b2(x) is the repair rate of unit 2; delta(.) is the Dirac-delta function.
Well-posedness of the above model and asymptotic behavior of its time-dependent solution have not been obtained until today.

accepted.question_text: For Su's 1997 system of supplementary-variable equations for a two dissimilar unit system with three modes and random checks, with state probabilities p0,0,k(x,t), p1,0,0(x,t), p0,1,0(x,t), p1,1,0(x,t), p0,1,1(x,t), p1,0,1(x,t), p0,2,0(x,t), p2,0,0(x,t), p1,1,1(x,t), p1,2,0(x,t), and p2,1,0(x,t); transition rates lambda1,0, lambda2,0, lambda0,1, lambda0,2; check rate alpha(x); and repair rates mu_i,0(x), mu_0,i(x), and mu_i,j(x), determine whether the full PDE system is well posed and determine the asymptotic behavior of its time-dependent solution.

evidence.quote: Where lambda1,0 is the failure rate of unit 1 from normal to partial failure; lambda2,0 is the failure rate of unit 1 from partial failure to total failure; lambda0,1 is the failure rate of unit 2 from normal to partial failure; lambda0,2 is the failure rate of unite 2 from partial failure to total failure; alpha(x) is the check rate satisfying alpha(x) >= 0 and its integral over [0, infinity) is infinity; mu_i,0(x) and mu_0,i(x) are repair rates for the two units; mu_i,j(x) is the repair rate when both units require repair.
Well-posedness of the system of the above equations and asymptotic behavior of its time-dependent solution have not been obtained until now.

accepted.question_text: For the two 2006 reliability models with state variables Q0(x,t) through Q4(x,t) and P0(x,t) through P6(x,t), representing systems attended by a repairman with vacations and involving boundary conditions such as Q0(0,t) = integral from 0 to infinity of alpha(x) Q0(x,t) dx + integral from 0 to infinity of mu(x) Q3(x,t) dx + delta(t) and P0(0,t) = integral from 0 to infinity of alpha(x) P0(x,t) dx + integral from 0 to infinity of mu(x) P3(x,t) dx + delta(t), where lambda is the working rate, mu(x) is the repair rate, and alpha(x) is the vacation rate of the repairman, determine whether these two PDE models are well posed and determine the asymptotic behavior of their time-dependent solutions when alpha(x) and mu(x) are non-constant functions.

evidence.quote: Here (x, t) in [x, infinity) x [0, infinity); Qi(x, t) (i = 0, 1, 2) is the probability that at time t the system is normal and the elapsed vacation time of repairman is x; Qi(x, t) (i = 3, 4) is the probability that at time t the system is down and the elapsed repair time of the piece is x; lambda is the working rate, mu(x) is the repair rate, alpha(x) is the vacation rate of the repairman, delta(.) is the Dirac-delta function.
When alpha(x) and mu(x) are non-constants, well-posendess and asymptotic behavior of the time-dependent solutions of the above two models have not been obtained until today.
